evidence: Cic. Att. 2.2.1: cūrā, amābō tē, Cicerōnem nostrum
terms.comment: With an accusative: a child, a patient, animals, plants. Corpus or sē cūrāre is to look after oneself with food and rest. For Cūrā ut valeās see take care.

evidence: Verg. A. 1.646: omnis in Ascaniō cārī stat cūra parentis
Plaut. Men. 897: cum cūrā magnā cūrābō
terms.comment: Also worry and concern (see care, about something).

phrases.english: Look after our little Cicero, please.

phrases.latin: ita ego eum cum cūrā magnā cūrābō tibi
phrases.english: So I’ll look after him for you with great care.
Now it’s time for food and rest.

phrases.latin: omnis in Ascaniō cārī stat cūra parentis
phrases.english: All his loving father’s care is fixed on Ascanius.

sources: Lewis & Short: curo · Lewis & Short: cura
